claim: The Nazi war economy kept the Fordist operation and placed it under a racial-juridical classification assigned by the state to populations taken in conquest.
quote: The Nazi war economy kept the verb. It took the Fordist operation, the task cut into motions and set to a time, and placed it under a noun of a new kind: a racial-juridical classification assigned by the state to whole populations taken in conquest.

claim: The paper follows the switch from conquest into the factory and marks where the murder of the Jews of Europe exceeds the history of labor.
quote: This half follows that switch from the conquest of the East into the factory, and marks the point where the history of labor ends and the murder of the Jews of Europe exceeds it.
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: The field holds Nazi expansion East a war for land and empire (Tooze: land hunger; 'the last great land grab').
quote: The field holds that Nazi expansion to the East was a war for land and empire. Adam Tooze: "Land hunger was one, if not the most important impulse"; the war in the East "was the last great land grab in the long and bloody history of European colonialism".
lineage: the East as a war for land and empire

claim: The camps came before the war and served repression first (USHMM).
quote: The camps came before the war and served repression first. USHMM: "The Nazi camp system began as a system of repression directed against political opponents of the Nazi state."

claim: Herbert: more than eight million foreign forced laborers in the Reich's war economy in 1944.
quote: Ulrich Herbert: "In 1944, more than eight million foreign forced laborers were employed in the German war economy inside the Reich."
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: Herbert: without foreign labor German production would have collapsed in 1942 at the latest.
quote: Ulrich Herbert: "In 1944, more than eight million foreign forced laborers were employed in the German war economy inside the Reich." And: "Without the use of foreign labor, the agricultural and industrial production of Germany would have collapsed in 1942 at the latest. The German war economy therefore had no choice but to depend on the employment of millions of forced laborers."
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: The forced-labor figures differ by denominator.
quote: The figures differ by denominator: the stock on a given date, the flow across the war, the Reich alone or the occupied territories with it.
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: USHMM's definition of the Holocaust.
quote: The Holocaust is defined by USHMM as "the systematic, state-sponsored persecution and murder of six million European Jews by the Nazi German regime and its allies and collaborators."
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: Gerwarth and Malinowski: the standard accounts give no colonial causation of Nazi anti-Jewish policy.
quote: the standard accounts of Nazi anti-Jewish policy, by Longerich, Browning and Friedländer, give no colonial causation, and the large literature on German antisemitism has not found colonial racism to be an influence.
lineage: no colonial or economic cause of the Holocaust

claim: The relation of labor to annihilation is disputed in the field (Kaienburg, Kárný; Pingel; Wagner).
quote: The relation of labor to annihilation is disputed. The phrase "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" entered policy language in the late-1942 negotiations of Goebbels and the Justice Minister Otto Thierack over the transfer of prisoners from the justice system to the SS camps; the SS did not generally use it, and it recurred at Nuremberg.[^12] Hermann Kaienburg and Miroslav Kárný treat annihilation through labor as a consistent SS goal; Falk Pingel holds that the phrase should not be applied to all prisoners; Jens-Christian Wagner calls it a metaphor of moral indignation, "not particularly helpful in an analytical sense".

claim: The colonial reading's three parts get different verdicts: the East as colonial empire least contested; continuity from South West Africa contested; colonial causation of the murder of the Jews largely rejected.
quote: The colonial reading of Nazism has three parts, and the field gives each a different verdict. (a) The East as colonial empire is the least contested.

claim: Continuity from German South West Africa is contested.
quote: (b) Continuity from German South West Africa is contested.

claim: The paper accepts the conventional reading whole; its object is the form of the labor relation built from conquest and the assembly line.
quote: This paper accepts all of 0.1–0.7. Its object is the form of the labor relation that the war economy built from conquest and the assembly line, read in the grammar of the first half: the noun, the verb, and the unit over which a person's capacity was measured.

claim: The Holocaust is larger than this labor history; the limit governs §9.
quote: The Holocaust is larger than this labor history. That limit governs §9.
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: Germany entered the Nazi period as an advanced industrial power; Fordism spread from 1936 (Hachtmann).
quote: Germany entered the Nazi period as an advanced industrial power. Hachtmann: "at the latest beginning in 1936 – and in marked contrast to the Weimar Republic – the Fordist production regime rapidly gained in significance in ever broader sectors of industry

claim: The East was also an answer to blockade (Table Talk).
quote: The East was also an answer to blockade. In the English *Table Talk*, 17–18 September 1941: "The struggle for the hegemony of the world will be decided in favour of Europe by the possession of the Russian space. Thus Europe will be an impregnable fortress, safe from all threat of blockade."
lineage: the East as a war for land and empire

claim: The English Table Talk is a weak text, to be checked against the German editions.
quote: The English edition is a weak text. It must be checked against the German editions

claim: Gordon: the Nazis failed to see the solution of moving labor out of agriculture; on this reading Lebensraum was the wrong answer.
quote: The Nazis "failed to see the obvious solution", which was to move labor out of agriculture; more land per farm worker could be had "Only by expelling" Polish farmers.

claim: Labor became a binding constraint; conquest delivered people to the factory, and the empire for land also became a mechanism for supplying labor.
quote: Lebensraum answered with land. What conquest delivered to the factory, from 1940 onward, was people. Labor became a binding constraint, and the empire pursued for land, settlement and racial reordering also became a mechanism for supplying it.

claim: The planners described the East in the vocabulary of overseas empire and the American West.
quote: The planners described the East in the vocabulary of overseas empire and the American West. USHMM: "Hitler and other Nazi thinkers drew direct comparisons to American expansion in the West"

claim: Inner colonization, an ethnically based settler colonialism, was older than Nazism (Nelson).
quote: The German term for the practice was older than Nazism. Robert Nelson: "The form of colonization that is central to this book is what was called 'inner colonization' at the time by German thinkers. This was an ethnically based settler colonialism powerfully grounded in agrarian thinking about who should cultivate what soil."

claim: Meyer drafted the first iteration of General Plan East: emptying the eastern space and filling it with German settlers.
quote: Nelson names "the new Settlement Commission, now the Reichskommisar für die Festigung deutschen Volkstums (RKF) led by Himmler", whose plans for the Warthegau "strongly echoed the 'border strip' plan of 1915".[^27] Konrad Meyer "pointed out that '*Raumenge*, restricted space, had long been Germany's problem, but that this was now solved.'"[^27] Meyer "penned what would be the first iteration of the infamous General Plan East … This plan, calling for the emptying of the eastern space, followed by its filling with German settlers"; he "declared that he would need 1.8 million German settlers."

claim: The continuity runs through an institution and its personnel (Meyer, the RKF); the doctrine's founder stands outside the deportations.
quote: The continuity runs through an institution and its personnel, Meyer and the RKF. The founder of the doctrine stands outside the deportations.

claim: Sandler: Eastern Europe offered readily accessible territory for colonial ambitions.
quote: Willeke Sandler: "While Africa remained a future possibility, Eastern Europe offered readily accessible territory for the fulfillment of colonial ambitions."

claim: The colonial relation was relocated from overseas to the continent.
quote: The colonial relation was relocated from overseas to the continent.

claim: Hachtmann: from 1941 the labour force was recruited as a kind of war booty from occupied Europe, unprotected by labour law.
quote: Hachtmann dates the change of labor supply to 1941: "the labour force subjected to these production regimes was increasingly recruited, above all from 1941 onward, as a kind of war booty from those territories of Europe occupied by the German military and was no longer protected by the usual labour laws of 'civil'-capitalist societies.

claim: USHMM: in August 1944 more than 7,500,000 non-German workers were registered in the Reich, the overwhelming majority forced laborers.
quote: "In August 1944, more than 7,500,000 non-German workers were registered as working in the Reich; the overwhelming majority were forced laborers."
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: Herbert: 7.6 million foreign workers in the Reich, 5.7 million civilians and a little under 2 million prisoners of war.
quote: "7.6 million foreign workers found themselves employed in the Reich: 5.7 million civilian workers and a little less than 2 million prisoners of war.
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: Herbert: the typical forced laborer in Germany in 1943 was an eighteen-year-old schoolgirl from Kiev.
quote: "The typical forced laborer in Germany in 1943 was an eighteen-year-old school girl from Kiev.
lineage: the war economy ran on foreign labor

claim: Recruitment ran along Spoerer's gradient of force, from advertising to deportation by arbitrary violence.
quote: Recruitment ran along a gradient of force. Spoerer distinguishes four ideal types: pure advertising; advertising backed by decisive pressure on living conditions; conscription of whole age cohorts through local administrations; and deportation by arbitrary violence.

claim: Territory and labor moved in opposite directions: the plan emptied the East, the labor program deported its people westward.
quote: Territory and labor moved in opposite directions.

claim: Herbert: forced foreign labor foreshadowed a racially ordered National Socialist society across the conquered continent.
quote: "The program of enforced foreign labor served to foreshadow what was slated to become everyday reality for all of Europe in the wake of a German victory…: namely, the installation throughout the conquered continent of a hierarchical National Socialist society founded on racial criteria."

claim: Conquest became labor policy: a chain from occupation through recruitment and deportation to registration, barracks and the plant.
quote: Conquest became labor policy. The chain runs from military occupation, through recruitment on Spoerer's gradient and deportation, to registration in the Reich, segregated barracks, and the plant.

claim: The colonial seizure of the East and the staffing of German industry became interlocking operations of one conquest regime.
quote: The colonial seizure of the East and the staffing of German industry became interlocking operations of the same conquest regime, coupled materially through occupation, deportation, registration and the plant.

claim: Hachtmann defines Fordism as rationalization and as a 'technology of domination', established under Nazi rule as 'war Fordism'.
quote: Hachtmann's abstract: "Fordism is understood here as a form of workplace rationalization (especially assembly-line production), but also as a 'technology of domination' and an 'exploitation innovation'. In contrast to the Weimar Republic, Fordism was established in broad sectors of German industry under Nazi rule in the form of 'war Fordism'."

claim: Hachtmann applies war Fordism from 1933; the production form preceded the camp labor that entered it.
quote: Hachtmann applies war Fordism from 1933: "The term 'war Fordism' – as a special form of Fordism – will thus be used here for the years starting in 1933

claim: The production form preceded the camp labor that entered it.
quote: The production form preceded the camp labor that entered it.

claim: Hachtmann: with full employment from 1934–35, organization that replaced qualified with unqualified workers became attractive.
quote: Forms of work organization and production technology that promised to replace qualified workers with unqualified ones thus became increasingly attractive.

claim: A job cut into operations can be staffed by whoever can perform one; after 1941 conquest supplied that worker.
quote: A job cut into operations can be staffed by whoever can perform one operation. After 1941 that worker was supplied by conquest.

claim: Hachtmann: camp prisoners were first used in regular industrial mass production from August 1942 at Heinkel, Oranienburg.
quote: "Prisoners from concentrations camps were used for the first time in 'regular' industrial mass production starting in August 1942 at the Heinkel aircraft plant in Oranienburg near the Sachsenhausen concentration camp.

claim: From October 1942 companies paid the Treasury 6 Reichsmarks a day for skilled prisoners, 4 for unqualified.
quote: "Beginning in October 1942, companies paid the Treasury 6 Reichsmarks per day for skilled prisoners and 4 Reichsmarks for unqualified"

claim: Hachtmann: prisoner deployment delayed automation; Fordism joined to extreme forced labour led to a dead end.
quote: Hachtmann: prisoner deployment "delayed the leap to (partial) automation", and "the connection between Fordism and extreme forced labour … thus led to a dead end."

claim: War Fordism decomposed work horizontally.
quote: War Fordism decomposed work horizontally. One process became a row of operations, each specified, timed and assigned to a station.

claim: Herbert: the contradiction of economic interest and racial ideology produced a rigidly hierarchical racist system for forced laborers.
quote: Herbert names the contradiction from which the labor order grew: "the contradiction between the economic interest in exploiting as many foreigners as possible and the ideological principles of National Socialism, which sought to protect the Volk from mixing with 'foreign blood.' From this contradiction there developed a rigidly hierarchical racist system for the treatment of forced laborers."

claim: Spoerer's ranking, Nordic peoples at the top, Jews and Sinti and Roma at the bottom; the regime for Poles and Ostarbeiter 'apartheid'.
quote: Spoerer gives the ranking: "Nordic" peoples at the top, then Romance peoples, then Slavic peoples, Poles and Soviet peoples, treated as "subhumans", with Jews and Sinti and Roma at the bottom. He calls the regime for Poles and Ostarbeiter "apartheid".

claim: Hachtmann: German male workers remaining in plants became racially privileged foremen and head workmen.
quote: Hachtmann: "from 1941 onward the core of the Fordist rationalization proletariat in Germany was constituted first and foremost by foreign labourers, especially male and female 'eastern labourers' from the Soviet Union (frequently replacing German women…). In contrast, male German workers, insofar as they remained in enterprises, advanced to become racially privileged foremen and head workmen."

claim: The racial state decomposed persons vertically; on one line the two cuts crossed.
quote: The racial state decomposed persons vertically. Fordism cut the process into operations; racial classification cut the workforce into grades. On one line the two cuts crossed.

claim: Hachtmann judges Roth's and Sofsky's opposed positions both exaggerated; camp labor was also economically functional for firms from 1942–43.
quote: Hachtmann quotes it as one extreme of the debate: "Karl-Heinz Roth occupies one extreme with his claim that 'slave labour can be used profitably even under the conditions of the most modern capitalist large-scale technology if it is incorporated solely into a workforce-pyramid racially organized in degrees of unfreedom'." Against it he sets Sofsky, for whom prisoner labor was "not a means of survival, but rather [a means] of absolute power and terror". Hachtmann: "Both positions are exaggerated. Despite the independent spiral of violence emphasized by Sofsky, the work deployment of concentration camp prisoners in industrial fabrication was, from the perspective of those companies using it, also quite functional economically, at least from 1942–1943 onward."

claim: Aptitude testing examined almost 500,000 foreign laborers; from autumn 1943 camp prisoners were tested individually.
quote: Hachtmann's complication is the aptitude test. "On the one hand, companies followed the hierarchy of 'races' prescribed by the Nazis, which ostensibly corresponded to the different work capacities of the labourers. On the other hand, certain aspects of workplace rationalization contributed to the fact that racism – brought into the work world by the Nazis from outside – was softened and carried out virtually ad absurdum." From 1941–42 the Institut für Arbeitspsychologie und Arbeitspädagogik ran tests for the "selection of foreigners" based on the American Army Alpha and Beta tests; "In the largest industrial psychological testing operation ever at the time, almost 500,000 civilian foreign labourers in far more than 1,000 companies were examined… Beginning in the autumn of 1943 concentration camp prisoners were even tested for their individual capabilities, irrespective of their national ('racial') affiliation and other categories."

claim: The testing tended to undermine the racist schema, and says little about the core issue.
quote: The testing "tended to undermine the racist schema", and it "says little about the core issue".

claim: The racial classification came from the state; production's own measures tended to disregard it; the state installed it anyway.
quote: The racial classification came from the state; the production system's own measures tended to disregard it; the state installed it anyway.

claim: Pohl to Himmler, 30 April 1942: the main emphasis of the camps has shifted to the economic side.
quote: Oswald Pohl to Himmler, 30 April 1942: "The war has brought about a marked change in the structure of the concentration camps and has changed their duties with regard to the employment of prisoners. The custody of prisoners for the sole purposes of security, education, or prevention is no longer the main consideration. The main emphasis has shifted to the economic side.

claim: Hachtmann: only a minority of camp prisoners were used in industrial production, and only from late 1942 to mid-1944.
quote: Hachtmann's scale caveat limits the term. "Only a minority of all prisoners in Nazi concentration camps was used in industrial production, and this took place exclusively during the relatively short time span from late 1942 to mid-1944.

claim: Herbert: in the war's first years camp-prisoner labor was of no importance to the war economy.
quote: "In the first years of the war, the work deployment of concentration camp prisoners was of no importance to the war economy"

claim: Allen: the satellite-camp network spread through the war economy only in 1944.
quote: A network of satellite camps did not spread throughout the German war economy until 1944, after which scarcely any German factory of importance had not applied for concentration camp prisoners.

claim: Campification defined: the attachment of the camp to the plant as an administrative unit (subcamp, supplier main camp, SS, contract).
quote: Campification, at the strength these figures carry, is the attachment of the camp to the plant as an administrative unit: a subcamp in or near the factory, supplied with prisoners by a main camp, run by the SS, and contracted to a firm.

claim: Camp prisoners were a small part of the foreign labor force: about 700,000 against about six million civilians and 2.2 million POWs at the peak.
quote: Camp prisoners were a small part of the foreign labor force: about 700,000 against about six million civilians and 2.2 million prisoners of war at the peak.

claim: The term names a form and its spread; the numbers set its weight.
quote: The term names a form and its spread. The numbers set its weight.

claim: The IG Farben tribunal: the camp was an important factor in choosing Auschwitz, and camp labor was planned from the beginning.
quote: We are satisfied after a thorough consideration of the evidence, that while the camp may not have been the determining factor in selecting the location, it was an important one and, from the beginning, it was planned to use concentration-camp labor to supplement the supply of workers.

claim: Hachtmann: camp prisoners lacked slave status in the classical sense, since the SS had little interest in maintaining their labour power.
quote: Hachtmann sets camp labor outside the slave form on exactly this ground. "The term 'slave labour' in this context has been largely avoided in the present article. … the concept can at best be used metaphorically. … Perhaps the most significant [objection] is the fact that these prisoners did not possess the status of 'slaves' in the classical sense, since slave owners usually had (and have) an interest in maintaining the labour power of the people under their control.

claim: USHMM: incarceration assured the labor supply while camp brutality depleted it; the SS used gas chambers to 'weed out' those unable to work.
quote: "The incarceration of increasing numbers of people in the concentration camps assured the quantity of the labor supply even as the brutality of life inside the camps depleted the number of available laborers. The SS used gas chambers and other means to 'weed out' prisoners who were no longer able to work."

claim: At Monowitz, after selections and mortality halved the camp, IG Farben obtained additional prisoners from the SS.
quote: To prevent such a sharp reduction in the number of prisoners available for labour to build the plant, I.G. Farben intervened at the highest SS levels to obtain additional prisoners.

claim: BASF: about 25,000 people died in connection with the IG Farben plant at Auschwitz-Monowitz, the vast majority Jewish inmates.
quote: "About 25,000 people died in connection with the IG Farben plant at Auschwitz-Monowitz. The vast majority were Jewish concentration camp inmates.

claim: The daily fee had the form of hire paid to a holder by confinement, without the chattel owner's capital loss: a third relation to the person.
quote: The daily fee had the form of hire, paid to a holder that held the body by confinement and did not bear the chattel owner's capital loss in the person as owned property at its death.

claim: At these sites the economic object was a flow: an allocation of persons per day, reduced by death and refilled by transport.
quote: The economic object at these sites was a flow: an allocation of persons per day, drawn from a captured population, reduced by death and refilled by transport.

claim: The slave-market analogy holds for the selection and fails for the asset.
quote: The analogy holds for the selection. For the asset it fails, since nobody bought the person.

claim: War Fordism kept the specified verb and made the noun a switch: classification selected the coercive regime.
quote: Slavery priced the noun. Fordism specified the verb. War Fordism kept the specified verb and made the noun a switch: racial-juridical classification selected the coercive regime under which the verb was extracted.

claim: USHMM: the ability to work offered Jews a chance of survival; those deemed unable were the first shot or deported.
quote: "the ability to work offered the chance of survival to Jews, for those deemed unable to work were the first to be shot or deported."

claim: The same act, reading productive capacity, had radically different consequences by juridical-racial status.
quote: The same general act, reading productive capacity, had radically different consequences depending on juridical-racial status.

claim: EVZ paid more than 1.66 million former forced laborers €4.4 billion, 2001–2007; the grading by category is to be verified.
quote: The EVZ Foundation paid more than 1.66 million former forced laborers in 98 countries a total of €4.4 billion between 2001 and 2007.

claim: Whether the payments were graded by the Nuremberg slave/forced distinction is an open verification item.
quote: The grading of the sums by category, and its match to the Nuremberg distinction, is to be verified.

claim: Within the range set by class, capacity, firm, workplace, sex, date and local administration also mattered.
quote: Within that range measured capacity, firm, workplace, sex, date and local administration also mattered, as Hachtmann's aptitude tests show (§5).

claim: Extermination is not reducible to optimization.
quote: Extermination is not reducible to optimization

claim: The regime destroyed labor it needed: the Soviet prisoners of war permitted to die in 1941–42.
quote: The regime destroyed labor it needed. The more than two million Soviet prisoners of war permitted to die in the autumn and winter of 1941–42 were destroyed before the decision to deploy Soviet prisoners as workers.

claim: For the Jews, labor deferred death and set no limit to it.
quote: For the Jews, labor deferred death and set no limit to it.

claim: Browning: the ideological goal was never superseded, only deferred; the destruction of Warsaw began in July 1942 regardless of productivity.
quote: Browning on the ghettos: the "productionists" wanted ghettoized Jews to work and sustain themselves, the "attritionists" saw the ghettos as a means of liquidation; when the productionists gained room, the ideological goal was "never superseded, just temporarily deferred". After the decision for the Final Solution the destruction of Warsaw began in July 1942 regardless of productivity.

claim: Hayes: the forced labor problem never really troubled the SS, dedicated to destruction as its overriding priority.
quote: Peter Hayes names the contradiction as a structural inefficiency. The regime was "constantly caught in contradictions that produced inefficiencies, encapsulated in this instance by the mutually negating desires to extract value from foreigners but to keep them separate from and unequal to the German population." "If—as Michael Allen has shown so well—that problem never really troubled the SS, which remained dedicated to destruction as its overriding priority, it did trouble the private industrial enterprises"

claim: Hayes: deprivation and death were omnipresent in the forced labor system and unequally distributed.
quote: "Deprivation and death were omnipresent in the Nazi forced labor system, but they were not equally distributed."

claim: Hayes: in many cases forced labor did not even pay for itself (Keller; Wagner on Monowitz's 15 percent).
quote: Forced labor did not always pay. Hayes: "in many cases, as Rolf Keller's paper shows, forced labor did not even pay for itself.
lineage: forced labor did not always pay

claim: Hayes qualifies his cases: not necessarily representative; involvement often had political and social causes.
quote: Hayes qualifies his cases: "These are not necessarily representative cases, but they point to something important: involvement in the slave labor system frequently had political and social causes rather than exclusively economic ones."
lineage: forced labor did not always pay

claim: Value explains why a firm took prisoners; access explains which firms got them.
quote: Value explains why a firm took prisoners; access explains which firms got them.
lineage: forced labor did not always pay

claim: Racial extermination and industrial exploitation sometimes reinforced each other and sometimes destroyed each other's objects.
quote: The two logics, racial extermination and industrial exploitation, sometimes reinforced each other and sometimes destroyed each other's objects.

claim: The Holocaust remains larger than this labor history: the murder of six million European Jews.
quote: The Holocaust remains larger than this labor history. It was the murder of six million European Jews.
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: The field finds the Holocaust's causes in Nazi anti-Jewish policy and gives it no colonial or economic cause.
quote: The field finds its causes in Nazi anti-Jewish policy and gives it no colonial or economic cause.
lineage: no colonial or economic cause of the Holocaust

claim: The labor history describes an industrial form the killing passed through at certain sites; it does not explain why the killing was done.
quote: The labor history in this paper describes an industrial form that the killing passed through at certain sites
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: It does not explain why the killing was done.
quote: It does not explain why the killing was done.
lineage: the Holocaust larger than the labor history

claim: Kramer: it is problematic to see the colonial camps as antecedents in a line ending at the Nazi death camps.
quote: Alan Kramer: "Concentration camps emerged in the violent imperial response to colonial liberation movements around the turn of the twentieth century: in Cuba (1895–8), the Philippines (1899–1902), South Africa (1899–1902), and German South West Africa (1904–7). The imperial powers drew on their own experience of counter-insurgency warfare as well as transnational knowledge transfer. Concentration camps became a byword for misery and mass death. Yet it is problematic to see the colonial camps as antecedents in a genealogical line at the end of which stand the Nazi death camps."

claim: Zimmerer, as Adhikari reports, points to continuities with the Nazi regime; 'From Windhoek to Auschwitz' is his phrase.
quote: Zimmerer's chapter, as Adhikari reports it, points "especially to continuities with the horrors perpetrated by the Nazi regime four decades later"; "From Windhoek to Auschwitz" is his phrase.

claim: Adhikari: an explanation of Nazi violence cannot simply be reduced to colonial influences.
quote: Adhikari: "Clearly an explanation of Nazi violence cannot simply be reduced to colonial influences."

claim: The paper takes Kramer's word: a common archive of concentration, captive labor, racial classification and settler clearance from about 1900.
quote: This paper takes Kramer's word. The repertoire of concentration, forced labor by captives, racial classification and settler clearance stood in a common archive from about 1900.

claim: No line of descent from Windhoek to the Nazi camps is claimed; the joining of camp and line belongs to 1942–44 and German industry.
quote: No line of descent from Windhoek to the Nazi camps is claimed here. The joining of the camp to the assembly line belongs to 1942–44 and to German industry.

claim: Arendt: continental imperialism allows no geographic distance between the methods of colony and nation; it 'truly begins at home'.
quote: its concept of cohesive expansion does not allow for any geographic distance between the methods and institutions of colony and of nation, so that it did not require boomerang effects in order to make itself and all its consequences felt in Europe. Continental imperialism truly begins at home.

claim: The colony entered the factory: conquest was metabolized at the industrial core.
quote: The colony entered the factory. Conquest was metabolized at the industrial core.

claim: Arendt judged the camps economically irrelevant; the paper extends her frame to labor and stops where §9 stops.
quote: Arendt does not carry her own frame into the labor relation. She judged the camps economically irrelevant.

claim: The argument claims Germany an advanced industrial power for which labor became a binding wartime constraint, and Lebensraum turned in practice into a labor supply.
quote: The argument claims that Germany was an advanced industrial power for which labor became a binding wartime constraint, and that Lebensraum, a land program on the American and British imperial model, was turned in practice into a labor supply

claim: Non-claims: camps not founded as labor institutions, camp labor not a large share, forced labor not generally profitable, no descent from the colonial camps, no economic or colonial cause of the Holocaust.
quote: It does not claim that the camps were founded as labor institutions, that camp labor was a large share of the war economy's workforce, that forced labor was generally profitable, that the Nazi camps descend from the colonial camps of 1900, or that the Holocaust has an economic or colonial cause.

claim: Industrial modernity kept radically unfree labor and learned to compose standardized production with graded human status.
quote: Industrial modernity kept radically unfree labor and learned to compose standardized production with graded human status.

claim: Tooze is quoted only through Gordon's review; his own pages unread.
quote: Tooze, *The Wages of Destruction*: quoted only through Gordon's review (pp. 166, 462); Tooze's own pages on the United States and the *Zweites Buch* unread.

claim: The 'Vernichtung durch Arbeit' positions are cited through Wikipedia.
quote: "Vernichtung durch Arbeit": origin and the Kaienburg, Kárný, Pingel and Wagner positions are cited through Wikipedia (citing Buggeln 2014)

claim: Arendt's judgment that the camps were economically irrelevant is cited through Wikipedia, to be located in the text.
quote: her judgment that the camps were economically irrelevant is cited through Wikipedia and to be located in the text.

claim: Relation to #1668: the first half followed the laboring body from noun to verb, plantation ledger to Ford line.
quote: The first half of this paper followed the laboring body from noun to verb: from the priced person of the plantation ledger to the timed operation of the Ford line.

claim: Relation to #923: the paper is retrospective analysis of the kind temporal sequestration says remains available.
quote: *Reflexive Foreclosure and the Worst-Case Surface*, §5, "temporal sequestration": a category "remains available for retrospective analysis but is inhibited when its criteria are applied to institutions operating in the present tense". This section is retrospective analysis of the kind the deposit says remains available. Its §6 criteria for campification (subcamp, supplier camp, contract, daily allocation) are stated so that they can be applied.

claim: Relation to #499: supplies the historical camp to which 'Semantic Labor Camp' refers.
quote: This section supplies the historical camp to which the term's name refers, and the case of an empire that classified populations before it set them to work (§§5, 8).

claim: Relation to #950: gives the naming its historical operation, the classification as switch.
quote: §8 here gives the naming its historical operation: the classification as switch, reading the verb to set the fate of the noun.

claim: Relation to #148: supplies the war form of the industrial-machinery parallel, the Fordist procedure staffed by conquered populations.
quote: This half supplies its war form: the Fordist procedure staffed by conquered populations (§4).

claim: Relation to #1545: the allocated day as a case where the laborer was carried on no books at all.
quote: §7 here is a case where the laborer was carried on no books at all: the allocated day, the prisoner replaced by transport.
